# Voice — self-hosted WebRTC voice chat for a Tailscale network

A small, dependency-light voice chat server for 2–6 phones in a room. The
Raspberry Pi only relays WebRTC signaling (SDP and ICE) over a WebSocket.
Audio is full-mesh peer-to-peer between the phones and never passes through
the Pi.

* Voice client: `https://100.87.117.55:9123`
* Admin panel: `https://100.87.117.55:9124`
* Storage: SQLite (WAL), all data in one file
* Runtime: Python 3 + `aiohttp` (from apt), no Node, no Docker, no build step
* Certificate: self-signed for the Tailscale IP, generated by `setup.sh`

```
 phone A  ────────────── audio (UDP, direct over Tailscale) ────────────── phone B
    │                                                                        │
    │  WSS signaling (SDP / ICE only)                     WSS signaling      │
    └──────────────────────────►  Pi :9123  ◄───────────────────────────────┘
                                   │
                          admin panel :9124
```

---

## 1. Project layout

```
voice/
  server.py            entrypoint: voice app :9123, admin :9124, TLS, retry bind
  config.json          bind IP, ports, cert paths, limits, ICE servers
  db.py                SQLite schema, helpers, settings overrides
  auth.py              scrypt hashing, sessions, CSRF, login throttling
  signaling.py         WebSocket rooms/peers + voice HTTP app
  admin_api.py         admin REST endpoints + admin static app
  manage.py            CLI: create-admin, reset-password, list-users, …
  setup.sh             idempotent installer for Raspberry Pi OS
  voice.service        systemd unit
  static/app/          index.html, app.js, style.css, manifest.json, sw.js, icons
  static/admin/        index.html, admin.js, style.css, favicon.svg
  README.md
```

The repository root is the application directory. On the Pi it lives at
`/home/gj/voice`.

---

## 2. Requirements

* Raspberry Pi Zero W (ARMv6, 512 MB) or anything better, Raspberry Pi OS.
* Python 3.9+ (tested on Raspberry Pi OS 13 "Trixie", Python 3.13).
* `python3-aiohttp`, `openssl`, `sqlite3` — installed by `setup.sh` from apt.
* Tailscale running on the Pi and on every phone, all in the same tailnet.
* The Pi's Tailscale IP. This build defaults to `100.87.117.55`; change it in
  `config.json` and in `allowed_origins` if yours differs.

The Pi listens on **only** `100.87.117.55:9123` and `:9124`. WebRTC media uses
random UDP ports directly between phones.

---

## 3. Install on the Pi

### 3.1 Get the files onto the Pi

From your computer (replace the path if you cloned elsewhere):

```bash
scp -r voice gj@100.87.117.55:/home/gj/voice
```

or, if the repository is on GitHub:

```bash
ssh gj@100.87.117.55
git clone https://github.com/alphingj/webrtc-voice-chat.git /home/gj/voice
```

### 3.2 Run the installer

```bash
ssh gj@100.87.117.55
cd /home/gj/voice
chmod +x setup.sh manage.py
sudo ./setup.sh
```

`setup.sh` is idempotent. It will:

1. `apt-get install python3-aiohttp openssl sqlite3 ca-certificates`
2. create `certs/` (mode 700), `static/app/icons/`, `static/admin/`
3. create a self-signed certificate valid 10 years with
   `subjectAltName = IP:100.87.117.55` (skipped if it already exists)
4. initialise `voice.db` (safe to run repeatedly)
5. install and enable `voice.service` (`User=gj`,
   `WorkingDirectory=/home/gj/voice`, `Restart=always`,
   `After=network-online.target tailscaled.service`)
6. restart the service and print the URLs

If the Tailscale IP is not up yet at boot, the server logs
`bind failed, retrying` and retries every 5 seconds until it can bind.

### 3.3 Create the first administrator

There is no default password. Run:

```bash
cd /home/gj/voice
python3 manage.py create-admin gjadmin
```

It prompts twice for a password (8+ characters). Then open the admin panel and
create users and rooms.

Useful CLI commands:

```bash
python3 manage.py list-users
python3 manage.py reset-password alice
python3 manage.py create-room "Living room" --max-participants 6
python3 manage.py list-rooms
python3 manage.py prune-audit --days 90
```

### 3.4 Open the apps on the phone

1. Connect the phone to Tailscale and confirm it can reach the Pi:
   `ping 100.87.117.55` (or use the Tailscale app's "Ping" action).
2. Open **`https://100.87.117.55:9123`** in Chrome.
3. Chrome shows `NET::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID` or "Your connection is not
   private". Tap **Advanced → Proceed to 100.87.117.55 (unsafe)**.
4. Sign in with the user the administrator created, or open an invite link.

> The certificate warning is expected: the certificate is self-signed. The
> page is still a secure context after you proceed, so the microphone works.
> Installing the certificate (§4) removes the warning and is required for a
> proper PWA install.

The admin panel is the same flow at **`https://100.87.117.55:9124`**.

---

## 4. Certificate warning, `thisisunsafe`, and Android trust

### 4.1 The quick bypass

* **Android Chrome:** tap **Advanced**, then **Proceed**.
* **Desktop Chrome:** on the interstitial, click the page background once and
  type `thisisunsafe` (no text box — just type it). The page reloads without
  the warning. This bypass is per-profile and can disappear after Chrome
  restarts.
* **Firefox:** **Advanced → Accept the Risk and Continue**.

The bypass is enough for voice. It is **not** enough for service-worker
registration on some Chrome versions, so "Install app" may only create a
shortcut. Install the certificate for a real PWA.

### 4.2 Download the certificate to the phone

The server publishes only the public certificate (never the key):

```
https://100.87.117.55:9123/server.crt
```

Open that URL in Chrome (accept the warning once) and download the file.

### 4.3 Install it on Android as a user CA

Android version menus differ slightly; the path is under Security:

1. **Settings → Security → More security settings → Encryption & credentials
   → Install a certificate → CA certificate → Install anyway.**
   (Android 11–14. On some devices: **Settings → Security → Advanced →
   Encryption & credentials**.)
2. Choose **Downloads** and select `voice-server.crt`.
3. Android warns that a third party may monitor traffic. This is your own
   certificate; accept.
4. Force-stop Chrome (or reboot the phone) and open
   `https://100.87.117.55:9123` again. The warning should be gone.

The certificate is generated with `basicConstraints=CA:TRUE` precisely so
Android will accept it as a user CA even though it is also the server
certificate. Android 7+ trusts user CAs in Chrome; some other apps do not.

### 4.4 `chrome://flags` fallback

If the microphone API is still missing (for example because you temporarily
serve the page over plain HTTP while debugging), you can whitelist the origin:

1. Open `chrome://flags/#unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure`.
2. Add `https://100.87.117.55:9123` (and `:9124` for the panel).
3. Set the flag to **Enabled**, relaunch Chrome.

This flag does **not** fix certificate errors — it only makes an otherwise
insecure origin count as secure. Use it as a last resort, not instead of
HTTPS.

---

## 5. Install the PWA

With the certificate trusted:

1. Open `https://100.87.117.55:9123` and sign in once.
2. Chrome menu → **Install app** (or **Add to Home screen**).
3. The icon opens standalone, keeps the session cookie, and the service worker
   caches only `/s/app.js`, `/s/style.css`, the manifest and the icons. HTML,
   API responses and WebSocket traffic are never cached.

The service worker is intentionally minimal: a new deploy is picked up on the
next load because assets are revalidated in the background. If you ever need to
force it, Chrome → Site settings → Clear & reset.

---

## 6. Using the admin panel

Open `https://100.87.117.55:9124` and sign in with the administrator account.

| Tab | What you can do |
|---|---|
| **Users** | Create users, edit username/role, disable/enable, delete, reset password, create one-time invite links |
| **Rooms** | Create, rename, delete, set max participants, set/remove a room password, choose "all users" or selected users, close/reopen |
| **Live** | See who is connected, in which room, for how long, with IP and mute state; force-mute or kick a peer; close a room |
| **Audit** | Filter by action or search actor/target/IP; entries auto-prune after the configured number of days |
| **Settings** | Max users/rooms/participants, session lifetimes, lockout policy, chat length, ICE servers, allowed origins |

Invite links look like
`https://100.87.117.55:9123/?invite=<token>`. The token is stored hashed and
is shown **once** when created. It creates one regular user account and then
expires (used or past its expiry).

Live admin actions reach existing sockets immediately:

* **Force-mute** sends `force-mute`; the client disables its own microphone
  and shows a banner.
* **Kick** sends `kicked`, closes the socket with code 4001, and broadcasts
  `peer-left` with reason `kicked_by_admin`.
* **Close room** marks the room closed, sends `room-closed`, closes code 4002,
  and refuses new joins until reopened.
* Disabling or deleting a user revokes their sessions and disconnects their
  live peers.

---

## 7. Configuration

`config.json` is read at startup. Relative paths are resolved against the
directory containing `server.py`.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `bind_ip` | `100.87.117.55` | Only this address is bound. Do not use `0.0.0.0`. |
| `voice_port` | `9123` | Voice app + WebSocket. |
| `admin_port` | `9124` | Admin panel + admin API. |
| `cert_file` | `certs/server.crt` | TLS certificate (PEM). |
| `key_file` | `certs/server.key` | TLS key (PEM, mode 600). |
| `db_path` | `voice.db` | SQLite database. |
| `static_dir` | `static` | Frontend files. |
| `max_users` | `50` | Account limit. |
| `max_rooms` | `20` | Room limit. |
| `max_participants_per_room` | `6` | Hard cap, also the per-room ceiling. |
| `session_lifetime_hours` | `72` | Voice app session. |
| `admin_session_lifetime_hours` | `12` | Admin session. |
| `ice_servers` | `[]` | Passed to `RTCPeerConnection`. Empty means pure host candidates over Tailscale. |
| `allowed_origins` | the two URLs | Exact HTTP origins allowed for API/WS requests. |
| `audit_retention_days` | `90` | Older audit rows are pruned. |
| `login_max_attempts` | `5` | Failures per IP/username before lockout. |
| `login_lockout_seconds` | `900` | Lockout and failure window. |
| `ws_max_message_bytes` | `65536` | Signaling message ceiling. |
| `ws_rate_limit_messages` | `120` | Messages per window per socket. |
| `ws_rate_limit_window_seconds` | `10` | Rate-limit window. |
| `ws_heartbeat_seconds` | `25` | WebSocket ping interval. |
| `bind_retry_seconds` | `5` | Retry delay when the Tailscale IP is absent. |
| `invite_max_hours` | `720` | Maximum invite lifetime. |
| `chat_max_length` | `500` | In-room text chat limit. |
| `log_level` | `INFO` | `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, … |
| `trust_proxy` | `false` | Honour `X-Forwarded-For` (leave off on Tailscale). |

Most limits can also be changed live in **Admin → Settings**; database values
override the file. `bind_ip`, ports, TLS paths and `trust_proxy` remain
file-only and need a restart.

If you change `bind_ip` or the ports, update `allowed_origins` to the exact
new URLs. The server also accepts its own `Host` origin, but the configured
list is authoritative.

---

## 8. Tailscale ACLs and firewall

### 8.1 ACL rules

With the default tailnet policy (`"src": ["*"], "dst": ["*:*"]`) everything
already works. If you restrict the tailnet, you need:

1. **Phones → Pi, TCP 9123 and 9124** for the app, admin panel and WebSocket.
2. **Phone ↔ phone, all UDP ports** (and TCP for fallback) for WebRTC media.
   ICE chooses random UDP ports; the Pi is not in the media path.

Example policy fragment (tags optional):

```json
{
  "tagOwners": {
    "tag:voice-server": ["autogroup:admin"],
    "tag:voice-users": ["autogroup:admin"]
  },
  "acls": [
    {
      "action": "accept",
      "src": ["tag:voice-users"],
      "dst": ["tag:voice-server:9123,9124"]
    },
    {
      "action": "accept",
      "src": ["tag:voice-users"],
      "dst": ["tag:voice-users:*"]
    }
  ]
}
```

The second rule is what allows the mesh: every phone must be able to reach
every other phone on the UDP port ICE picked. Do not restrict it to 9123/9124.

### 8.2 ufw on the Pi

```bash
sudo ufw allow in on tailscale0 to any port 9123 proto tcp
sudo ufw allow in on tailscale0 to any port 9124 proto tcp
sudo ufw reload
sudo ufw status verbose
```

No UDP ports need to be opened on the Pi for media. Do **not** open 9123/9124
on `eth0` or `wlan0`.

---

## 9. Certificates

### 9.1 Regenerate (new IP, expiry, or lost key)

```bash
cd /home/gj/voice
sudo systemctl stop voice
sudo openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -sha256 -days 3650 -nodes \
  -keyout certs/server.key -out certs/server.crt \
  -subj "/CN=100.87.117.55" \
  -addext "subjectAltName=IP:100.87.117.55" \
  -addext "basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE" \
  -addext "keyUsage=critical,digitalSignature,keyEncipherment,keyCertSign" \
  -addext "extendedKeyUsage=serverAuth"
sudo chown gj:gj certs/server.crt certs/server.key
sudo chmod 600 certs/server.key
sudo systemctl start voice
```

Then re-install `https://100.87.117.55:9123/server.crt` on each phone (Android
keeps the old CA until you remove it in **Security → Encryption &
credentials → User credentials**).

Check the SAN:

```bash
openssl x509 -in /home/gj/voice/certs/server.crt -noout -text | grep -A1 "Subject Alternative Name"
```

### 9.2 Why not Tailscale HTTPS?

`tailscale cert` requires HTTPS support on the tailnet. If your account returns
"does not support getting TLS certs", this self-signed certificate is the
fallback. The hostname form `https://voice.tailnet-name.ts.net` is not used.

---

## 10. Backup and restore

The database uses WAL mode. Use SQLite's backup command while the service is
running; copying the file alone can miss the `-wal` contents.

```bash
sudo -u gj sqlite3 /home/gj/voice/voice.db \
  ".backup '/home/gj/voice-backup-$(date +%F).db'"
```

Back up these too:

```bash
sudo tar czf /home/gj/voice-config-$(date +%F).tar.gz \
  -C /home/gj/voice config.json certs
```

Restore:

```bash
sudo systemctl stop voice
sudo -u gj cp /path/to/backup.db /home/gj/voice/voice.db
sudo rm -f /home/gj/voice/voice.db-wal /home/gj/voice/voice.db-shm
sudo chown gj:gj /home/gj/voice/voice.db
sudo systemctl start voice
```

---

## 11. Operations

```bash
sudo systemctl status voice
sudo systemctl restart voice
sudo journalctl -u voice -f          # structured JSON lines
sudo journalctl -u voice --since "1 hour ago"
```

Logs are one JSON object per line with `ts`, `level`, `msg`, and fields such as
`event`, `peer`, `user`, `ip`, `port`. `systemctl stop` sends SIGTERM; the
server closes sockets with code 1012 and exits cleanly.

Upgrade:

```bash
cd /home/gj/voice
git pull
sudo ./setup.sh
```

`setup.sh` keeps the certificate and database.

Expected resources: roughly 35–55 MB RSS idle and well under 80 MB with six
connected peers, because the Pi handles only a few JSON messages per
connection. CPU is near idle between heartbeats. Check with:

```bash
systemctl show voice -p MemoryCurrent
```

---

## 12. Manual test plan

You need three Android phones on the tailnet, three accounts, and one room
(max participants ≥ 3).

1. **Accounts:** as admin, create `alice`, `bob`, `carol`; create a room
   "Test"; create an invite; register a fourth user with the invite and confirm
   the same link is rejected the second time.
2. **Join:** open `https://100.87.117.55:9123` on each phone, accept the
   certificate, sign in, join "Test". Each phone shows all three names.
3. **Audio:** speak on phone A; B and C hear it and A's avatar shows the
   speaking ring. Repeat for B and C. Mute A; B and C see "muted" and hear
   silence. Unmute.
4. **Volume:** drag B's slider on A to 20%; B becomes quieter only on A.
5. **Push to talk:** enable PTT on C; C is silent until the hold bar is
   pressed; the speaking ring appears only while held.
6. **Admin live:** open the panel on a fourth device. Live shows three peers,
   durations and rooms. Force-mute B: B's mic disables and a banner appears.
   Kick C: C returns to the lobby with a message; A and B see C leave.
7. **Disabled user:** disable A in the admin panel. A's live socket closes and
   a new login fails with "Invalid username or password".
8. **Network drop:** turn Wi-Fi off on B for 10 seconds, then on. B shows
   "reconnecting" and rejoins automatically; A and C see B leave and rejoin.
9. **Refresh:** reload B mid-call. It rejoins the same room without manual
   action.
10. **Room close:** close the room from Live. Everyone is returned to the
    lobby and cannot rejoin until it is reopened.
11. **Screen lock:** lock a phone for two minutes, unlock, confirm audio still
    flows (see §13.4 for Android caveats).
12. **Reboot:** `sudo reboot` the Pi. After boot the service binds when
    `tailscale0` is up; phones reconnect with backoff and rejoin.

### Acceptance checklist

- [ ] Three phones in one room hear each other in both directions.
- [ ] Speaking indicators work for local and remote audio.
- [ ] Mute, per-peer volume and push-to-talk work.
- [ ] Admin can force-mute and kick a live peer; effects are immediate.
- [ ] A disabled user cannot sign in, and existing sessions are revoked.
- [ ] A refresh or short network drop rejoins the room automatically.
- [ ] Closing a room disconnects everyone and blocks new joins.
- [ ] The audit log records logins, failures, joins/leaves and admin actions.
- [ ] The server starts after a reboot without manual steps.
- [ ] `https://…:9123/api/health` returns `{"ok": true}` and the admin API is
      **not** present on 9123.
- [ ] No listener on `0.0.0.0`; only `100.87.117.55:9123` and `:9124`.

## 13. Troubleshooting

### 13.1 `navigator.mediaDevices` is undefined

`getUserMedia` requires a secure context. Causes, in order of likelihood:

1. The page was opened as `http://…` instead of `https://…`.
2. A certificate error page is still showing; the page never loaded.
3. The browser is old or the PWA was installed from an HTTP origin.
4. Chrome's site permission for the microphone is blocked.

Fix: open `https://100.87.117.55:9123` exactly, accept the certificate
(§4), reload. In Chrome: **⋮ → Settings → Site settings → Microphone** and make
sure the origin is allowed. The app shows a red banner at boot when the API is
missing, and a specific message on login if permission is denied.

### 13.2 Everyone is connected but there is no audio

* Tap the yellow **Tap to enable audio** banner — Chrome blocks autoplay
  until a gesture.
* Check the phone's media volume and whether audio is routed to Bluetooth.
* Check the mute state in the participant list and the admin Live view.
* Make sure the per-peer volume slider is not at 0.
* Open `chrome://webrtc-internals` on one phone and look at the
  `RTCPeerConnection` entries: `connectionState` should become `connected`
  and the audio `outbound-rtp` bitrate should be around 24–32 kbps.
* Confirm both phones are in the same tailnet and can ping each other:
  `tailscale status`, then `tailscale ping <other-phone-ip>`.
* If one phone uses a restrictive network that blocks direct UDP, Tailscale
  falls back to DERP relay. Audio still works (higher latency). See §13.3.

### 13.3 Tailscale relay (DERP) vs direct

```bash
tailscale status            # look for "direct" vs "relay"
tailscale ping 100.x.y.z    # prints "via DERP(...)" or "via 192.0.2.1:41641"
tailscale netcheck          # NAT type, UDP support, nearest DERP
```

* `direct` is what you want: media goes phone-to-phone over WireGuard.
* `relay "fra"` means the WireGuard packets go through a DERP server. Media is
  still end-to-end encrypted and still works; latency is higher. If audio
  breaks only on relay, suspect an ACL rule that allows TCP 9123/9124 but not
  UDP between clients.
* Tailscale tries direct connections continuously; `tailscale ping` after a
  minute often flips to direct. Enabling UPnP/NAT-PMP on the router, or
  allowing outbound UDP, helps.

### 13.4 Android suspends the microphone when the screen locks

Android may suspend a background tab and stop the microphone. The app takes a
Screen Wake Lock while it is in a room, and re-acquires it on
`visibilitychange`, but the wake lock is released when the page is hidden or
the browser is backgrounded.

Mitigations:

* Keep the page visible; use **Push to talk** so brief screen-off periods do
  not hold an open mic.
* Disable battery optimisation for Chrome:
  **Settings → Apps → Chrome → Battery → Unrestricted**.
* Keep the phone charging and the screen timeout long while testing.
* Use a Bluetooth headset; some phones keep the SCO link alive with the screen
  off, but Chrome may still pause the tab.
* If audio dies after unlock, reload the page — the app rejoins automatically,
  or use the in-page reconnect (it retries with backoff).

### 13.5 The service does not start / bind fails

```bash
sudo journalctl -u voice -n 50 --no-pager
ip -4 addr show tailscale0
```

* `bind failed, retrying` with `Cannot assign requested address`: the Tailscale
  IP is not up yet. The server retries; check `systemctl status tailscaled`.
* `TLS certificate missing`: run `sudo ./setup.sh`, or regenerate (§9.1).
* `Address already in use`: something else holds 9123/9124 —
  `sudo ss -ltnp | grep -E '9123|9124'`.
* Service exits immediately: run it in the foreground to see the traceback:
  `sudo -u gj python3 /home/gj/voice/server.py --config /home/gj/voice/config.json`.

### 13.6 Login loops or "session expired"

Sessions are server-side and expire after `session_lifetime_hours`. Changing a
password, disabling a user or deleting a user revokes them. Clear the site
cookie for the origin and sign in again. Check the audit log for
`login_failed` / `login_locked`; a lockout lasts `login_lockout_seconds`.

### 13.7 Admin panel says unauthorized on 9123

By design. The admin API exists only on 9124. The two cookies have different
names and scopes (`voice_sid` for the app, `voice_admin_sid` for the panel);
an app session cannot be used on the admin API even though cookies are shared
across ports of the same host.

---

## 14. Security notes

* No default accounts. The first admin is created from the CLI.
* Passwords: scrypt (N=8192, r=8, p=1, 16-byte random salt), constant-time
  comparison, per-password salt. Roughly 0.3–0.6 s on a Pi Zero W.
* Sessions: 32-byte random tokens, only SHA-256 hashes stored, server-side
  expiry, `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax` cookies.
* CSRF: state-changing requests require `X-CSRF-Token` matching the session's
  token in SQLite. Login/registration validate the `Origin` header.
* Login throttling per IP and per username, with lockout and audit entries.
* WebSocket upgrades require a valid app-scoped session and an allowed
  `Origin`; message rate and size limits apply per socket.
* All SQL uses parameters; all user-supplied strings are validated.
* CSP is `default-src 'self'` with no inline scripts or styles; the frontends
  are plain external JS/CSS.
* Admin API and voice API are separate aiohttp applications on separate ports;
  admin routes return 404 on 9123.
* Signaling is relay-only: the Pi never decodes or records audio. Media is
  DTLS-SRTP between phones.
* The public certificate is downloadable at `/server.crt`; the private key is
  never served.

---

## 15. Protocol reference (for debugging)

### 15.1 WebSocket

Connect: `wss://100.87.117.55:9123/ws` with the `voice_sid` cookie (or
`?token=<session token>`). Origin must be allowed.

Client → server:

```json
{"type":"join","room_id":1,"password":"optional","muted":false}
{"type":"leave"}
{"type":"offer","to":"<peer_id>","sdp":{"type":"offer","sdp":"v=0..."}}
{"type":"answer","to":"<peer_id>","sdp":{"type":"answer","sdp":"v=0..."}}
{"type":"candidate","to":"<peer_id>","candidate":{"candidate":"...","sdpMid":"0","sdpMLineIndex":0}}
{"type":"mute","muted":true}
{"type":"chat","text":"hello"}
{"type":"ping"}
```

Server → client:

```json
{"type":"hello","peer_id":"...","user":{...},"ice_servers":[],"limits":{...}}
{"type":"joined","you":"...","room":{...},"peers":[...],"ice_servers":[]}
{"type":"peer-joined","peer":{...}}
{"type":"peer-left","peer_id":"...","username":"...","reason":"left|disconnected|kicked_by_admin|timeout"}
{"type":"offer","from":"...","sdp":{...}}
{"type":"answer","from":"...","sdp":{...}}
{"type":"candidate","from":"...","candidate":{...}}
{"type":"mute-state","peer_id":"...","muted":true}
{"type":"force-mute","by":"admin"}
{"type":"chat","from":"...","username":"...","text":"...","ts":0}
{"type":"kicked","reason":"...","message":"..."}
{"type":"room-closed","reason":"...","message":"..."}
{"type":"error","code":"...","message":"..."}
{"type":"pong","ts":0}
```

Negotiation rule: the **newcomer offers** to every peer in `joined.peers`.
Existing peers only answer. ICE candidates are buffered until the remote
description is set. On `failed`, the original offerer rebuilds the peer
connection after 2 s; the other side accepts the new offer.

### 15.2 HTTP API

Voice (port 9123):

```
POST /api/login       {username,password}         -> {user,csrf}
POST /api/register    {token,username,password}   -> {user,csrf}
POST /api/logout
GET  /api/me
GET  /api/rooms
GET  /api/health
GET  /server.crt
```

Admin (port 9124, admin session + CSRF on writes):

```
POST   /api/login
POST   /api/logout
GET    /api/me
GET    /api/users                 POST /api/users
PATCH  /api/users/{id}            DELETE /api/users/{id}
POST   /api/users/{id}/password
GET    /api/invites               POST /api/invites
DELETE /api/invites/{id}
GET    /api/rooms                 POST /api/rooms
PATCH  /api/rooms/{id}            DELETE /api/rooms/{id}
PUT    /api/rooms/{id}/access
POST   /api/rooms/{id}/close      POST /api/rooms/{id}/open
GET    /api/live
POST   /api/live/{peer_id}/kick   POST /api/live/{peer_id}/mute
GET    /api/audit?limit&offset&action&q
GET    /api/settings              PUT /api/settings
```

Errors are `{"error":"code","message":"human text"}` with a matching HTTP
status.
